title: Champollion Method Card
description: Describes a translation method's architecture, components, and provenance. Embedded in run_cards at publish time and displayed on the leaderboard. Independent of the plugin manifest — a method card describes HOW a method works; a plugin manifest describes HOW TO INSTALL it.

name.description: Human-readable method name (e.g., 'FST-Gated Coached Pipeline v7').

class.description:
Primary method class. Determines how the method is categorized on the leaderboard.

- direct-llm: Single LLM call with a system prompt
- coached-llm: LLM with language-specific coaching data injected into context
- api-translation: Commercial translation API (Google, DeepL, Microsoft, etc.)
- rule-based: Finite-state transducers, grammar rules, morphological analyzers
- hybrid-pipeline: Multi-stage combining 2+ method classes (e.g., LLM + FST validation)
- human-in-the-loop: Human post-editing or validation in the pipeline
- ensemble: Multiple models/methods with voting or selection
- fine-tuned: Fine-tuned or adapted model (LoRA, QLoRA, full fine-tune)
- dictionary-augmented: Translation augmented with bilingual dictionary lookup
- community-reviewed: Translation produced by any method then reviewed by community speakers

paradigm.description: MT paradigm — the algorithmic approach, ORTHOGONAL to `class` and to the dependency class. Makes rule-based vs statistical vs neural vs LLM comparable on the leaderboard regardless of class (e.g. Apertium = rule-based, Google/OPUS-MT = neural-nmt, a raw GPT call = llm, an FST-gated LLM = hybrid). Optional; absent is treated as 'unknown'. Enforced by the harness (config.VALID_PARADIGMS) and recorded as the run_cards.paradigm column on publish.

version.description: Semver or major.minor version of this method (e.g., '7.2', '1.0.0').

description.description: Human-readable description of the method's approach, key innovations, and design rationale. This is displayed on the leaderboard detail panel.

author.description: Who developed and tested this method. May be a person, team, or organization.

contact.description: Contact email for questions about this method.

url.description: URL for the method's documentation, paper, or repository.

target_languages.description: CLDR locale codes this method was designed and validated for. A method might generalize beyond these, but these are the languages with explicit testing.

language_agnostic.description: If true, the method makes no language-specific assumptions. Most LLM-based and API methods are language-agnostic. FST-based and coached methods are typically language-specific.

pipeline.description: Ordered list of processing stages. For single-stage methods, this is a one-element array. For hybrid pipelines, each stage describes one component.

model.description: Primary model used. For ensemble methods, use the 'models' array instead.

models.description: All models used in ensemble or multi-stage methods.

tools_used.description: List of tools, libraries, APIs, or resources used (e.g., 'GiellaLT FST', 'sacrebleu', 'itwêwina dictionary', 'Google Translate API'). Displayed as tags on the leaderboard.

tools_enabled.description: Whether the LLM was given access to tool-calling (function calling) during translation.

coaching.description: Coaching data configuration. Only applicable for coached-llm and hybrid-pipeline methods.

fst.description: Finite-state transducer configuration. Only applicable for rule-based and hybrid-pipeline methods.

post_processing.description: Post-processing steps applied after translation (e.g., script conversion, morphological repair, formatting normalization).

quality_control.description: Quality control mechanisms used in the method.

data_sovereignty.description: Data sovereignty and ethical considerations. Especially important for Indigenous and endangered language methods.

dependency_class.description:
Effective dependency class — the most restrictive class among the method's declared dependencies (order S < O < A1 < A2 < X).

- S: self-contained — all code/data/weights ship in the method directory under licenses permitting redistribution and community transfer
- O: open external — externally hosted open-licensed artifacts (incl. copyleft), pinned and mirrored into the submission
- A1: substitutable LLM inference at runtime, via the sandbox LLM gateway; the model is interchangeable configuration
- A2: non-substitutable external data/service API (e.g., an API serving unlicensed proprietary content); flagged 'external dependency' on the leaderboard, not prize-eligible until rights holder permissions exist
- X: bundles content the submitter has no right to include; inadmissible

Drives sandbox runnability and prize eligibility. Canonical definitions: arena Method Interface spec, 'Method Validity and Dependency Classes'.

dependencies.description: Dependency manifest: every external artifact or service the method requires at install or runtime, with license and access mode. The harness derives the effective dependency_class from this list; a mismatch with the declared dependency_class is a validation error. An empty array is an affirmative declaration of Class S.

open_source.description: Whether the method's code, prompts, and coaching data are publicly available.

license.description: SPDX license identifier or license description (e.g., 'MIT', 'CC-BY-NC-4.0', 'community-controlled').

reproducibility.description:
How reproducible this method is.

- full: Deterministic with fixed random seed, same code produces same output
- partial: Same approach but LLM non-determinism means outputs vary
- non-reproducible: Requires specific hardware, proprietary data, or human intervention

limitations.description: Known limitations, failure modes, or caveats (e.g., 'Struggles with long-distance morphological agreement', 'No support for mixed-script input').

notes.description: Free-form notes from the method author.

model.description: Model used in this stage (if applicable).

fallback.description: What happens if this stage fails (e.g., 'pass-through', 'retry-with-different-model', 'reject').

slug.description: OpenRouter model slug or equivalent identifier (e.g., 'google/gemini-2.5-flash', 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4').

context_window.description: Effective context window size used (may be smaller than model max).

fine_tuned.description: Whether this is a fine-tuned variant.

fine_tune_details.description: Details about fine-tuning: base model, dataset size, technique (LoRA, QLoRA, full).

type.description: How coaching data is injected into the translation process.

sources.description: Where coaching data comes from (e.g., 'community elders', 'published grammars', 'morphological paradigms').

example_count.description: Number of translation examples in the coaching data.

includes_grammar.description: Whether coaching data includes explicit grammar rules or paradigm tables.

includes_glossary.description: Whether coaching data includes a bilingual glossary.

community_approved.description: Whether the coaching data has been reviewed and approved by community language authorities.

version.description: Version or commit of the FST analyzer.

role.description:
How the FST is used in the pipeline.

- validator: Checks morphological validity of output (accept/reject)
- generator: Generates morphologically correct forms
- gate: Blocks invalid output and triggers retry
- post-processor: Repairs morphological errors in output

coverage.description: Estimated lexical coverage of the FST analyzer (e.g., '~85% of everyday vocabulary').

retries_on_failure.description: Whether the method retries failed translations with different parameters.

max_retries.description: Maximum number of retries per entry.

fallback_strategy.description: What happens when all retries fail (e.g., 'return-best-attempt', 'return-empty', 'flag-for-review').

kind.description: What the dependency is: a dataset/dictionary (data), model weights or hosted inference (model), a library/tool (software), or a remote API (service).

license.description: SPDX license identifier, 'proprietary', or 'none'. 'none' means no public license exists — treated as all-rights-reserved.

access.description:
How the method obtains the dependency.

- bundled: ships inside the method directory
- mirrored: fetched at install time from an external host, pinned, and vendored into the submission
- gateway: runtime LLM inference routed through the sandbox evaluation gateway
- external-api: any other runtime network call

source.description: Canonical URL or 'provider:slug' identifier for the artifact or endpoint.

pin.description: Version, commit, or content hash pinning the exact artifact. Required for access mode 'mirrored'.

substitutable.description: For 'gateway'/'external-api' access: whether any compatible endpoint can serve this dependency (true distinguishes Class A1 from A2). A method depending on provider-side state (provider-hosted fine-tunes, file stores) is not substitutable.

redistributable.description: Whether the license permits redistributing the artifact (e.g., mirroring it into a sandbox submission).

transferable.description: Whether the artifact, or rights sufficient for community use/modification/redeployment, can convey to a language community's governance organization under prize transfer terms.

notes.description: Free-form context (e.g., rights-holder status, pending permission asks).

principles.description: Data sovereignty frameworks this method respects.

community_consent.description: Whether the relevant language community has consented to this method's use of their language data.

data_stays_local.description: Whether all language-specific data remains on-premise (not sent to cloud APIs).
